title: Molecular Jets from an Evolved Protostar: Insights from JWST-ALMA Synergy
question: How do the cold (ALMA CO, SiO) and warm/hot (JWST/MIRI H2 rotational) gas in the HOPS 315 (G205S3) jet and outflow compare in morphology and physical conditions (temperature, extinction, mass-loss rate)?

what.value: Bolometric temperature Tbol = 180 +/- 33 K, Lbol = 6.4 +/- 2.4 Lsun and spectral index ~0.417 of HOPS 315

evidence.quote: is a Class I protostellar system characterized by a bolometric temperature of $T_{\mathrm{bol}} = 180 \pm 33$ K

what.value: Inclination angle 40 +/- 8 deg from the CO outflow morphology

evidence.quote: The inclination angle for G205S3 was estimated to be $40\ensuremath{^\circ} \pm 8\ensuremath{^\circ}$ based on the wide-angle CO outflow morphology observed with ALMA

what.value: Mean jet velocity ~125 km/s and ALMA jet mass-loss rates (total ~0.59e-6 Msun/yr; blue lobe 0.29 +/- 0.12 e-6 Msun/yr)

evidence.quote: and a mean jet velocity of $\sim 125\ km\ s^{-1}$

what.value: Wavelength-dependent JWST/MIRI PSF FWHM relation 0.033 (lambda/um) + 0.106 arcsec

evidence.loc: 3.3 Combining ALMA Maps with JWST Observations
evidence.quote: the PSF FWHM is estimated using the relation $\theta_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = 0.033\,(\lambda/\mu\mathrm{m}) + 0.106\ensuremath{''}$

what.value: Weingartner & Draine mid-infrared extinction curve used for the extinction correction

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Extinction Correction in H2 Rotational Diagram Analysis
evidence.quote: extinction curve for the mid-infrared regime to correct extinction to the observed fluxes

what.value: Terminal jet velocity of 120-125 km/s from JWST infrared observations (comparison)

evidence.quote: derived a terminal jet velocity of 120-125 km s$^{-1}$ based on JWST infrared observations

recipe.goal: Image ALMA SiO, CO and continuum
recipe.method: Calibrate with the standard CASA pipeline and image with tclean at robust +2.0; bin line cubes to 2.0 km/s

recipe.goal: Detect bright emission lines in JWST/MIRI cubes
recipe.method: peakmoment first stage: extract spectra from a 0.5'' radius aperture on the jet, smooth, find local maxima and keep peaks above 5-7 sigma
Per line, take a subcube, fit a pixel-wise polynomial to line-free channels, subtract it and compute moment-0 from channels above 3 sigma of the residual
key_parameters: Spectral window +/-0.1-0.2 um of line-free channels; exclude +/-0.014-0.02 um around the peak; polynomial order up to 2

recipe.goal: Overlay ALMA maps on JWST maps
recipe.method: Resample ALMA maps onto the JWST pixel grid with bilinear interpolation, keeping native beams, and overlay SiO contours on JWST moment maps

recipe.goal: Derive H2 excitation temperatures, A_V and column densities
recipe.method: Rotational (Boltzmann) diagram of MIRI H2 0-0 lines from a 0.5'' aperture on knot B2; A_V from ortho/para line-flux ratios; extinction-corrected single- and two-temperature fits
key_parameters: Linear fit of ln(Nu/gu) vs Eu gives slope -1/Tex
assumptions: LTE and optically thin H2 lines
Weingartner & Draine mid-IR extinction curve with A_V = 23.3 mag

recipe.method: Cylindrical-flow model of the molecular jet with mean N(H2), constant velocity and jet width equal to the MIRI PSF FWHM at 5.5 um
assumptions: mu_H2 = 2.8; jet unresolved so width set by PSF

recipe.goal: Compare knot positions and dynamical ages between ALMA and JWST
recipe.method: Compute knot dynamical ages from jet velocity, inclination and Orion distance; measure offset between JWST H2 peaks and the ALMA SiO Gaussian centroid of knot B2; compare with expected proper motion over 4.37 yr
assumptions: Jet velocity 125 km/s, inclination 40 deg, distance 400 pc

answer_key.quantity: Visual extinction A_V toward the jet near the continuum peak

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Extinction Correction in H2 Rotational Diagram Analysis
evidence.quote: We have estimated an mean visual extinction A$_V$ = 23.3$\pm$2.5 mag from the observed integrated line flux ratios of ortho-to-para.

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Extinction Correction in H2 Rotational Diagram Analysis
evidence.quote: A single-temperature fit yields a rotational temperature of 1023 $\pm$ 67 K, consistent with a warm molecular component.

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Extinction Correction in H2 Rotational Diagram Analysis
evidence.quote: we also performed a two-temperature fit, resulting in T$_\mathrm{1}$=773$\pm$44 K and T$_\mathrm{2}$=2499$\pm$721 K.

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Extinction Correction in H2 Rotational Diagram Analysis
evidence.quote: we also performed a two-temperature fit, resulting in T$_\mathrm{1}$=773$\pm$44 K and T$_\mathrm{2}$=2499$\pm$721 K.

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Extinction Correction in H2 Rotational Diagram Analysis
evidence.quote: we derive column densities of $N_1 = (3.34 \pm 0.43 \times 10^{20}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ for temperature component $T_1$, and $N_2 = (1.11 \pm 1.03) \times 10^{19}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$ for $T_2$.

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Extinction Correction in H2 Rotational Diagram Analysis
evidence.quote: The combined mean molecular hydrogen column density is estimated to be $N(\mathrm{H}_2) = (1.72 \pm 0.22) \times 10^{20}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Combined N(H2), Summary value (inconsistent with Section 3.2.1)

evidence.quote: The combined molecular hydrogen column density is $N(\mathrm{H}_2) = (3.48 \pm 1.02) \times 10^{20}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Jet mass-loss rate, blueshifted lobe, from JWST

evidence.quote: We estimate a jet mass-loss rate of $\dot{M}_{\rm J, blue, JWST} \approx 0.27 \times 10^{-6} \pm 0.2 \times 10^{-6}~M_\odot~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: Jet mass-loss rate, total (2x blue lobe), from JWST
Dynamical ages of knots B1 and B2
answer_key.value: B1 ~10 yr at ~210 AU; B2 ~30 yr at ~630 AU

evidence.quote: the dynamical age of knot B1 is estimated to be $\sim$10 years at a projected separation of $\sim$ 210 AU, while knot B2 is $\sim$30 years old at $\sim$ 630 AU.

answer_key.quantity: Offset between JWST H2 peak and ALMA SiO centroid of knot B2

evidence.quote: The positional offset between the JWST/MIRI H$_2$ emission at shorter wavelengths and the ALMA SiO Gaussian centroid of knot B2 ranges from $\sim$ 0.45$''$ at 5.51 $\mu$m to 0.26$''$ at 9.665 $\mu$m.

answer_key.quantity: Expected knot displacement over the 4.37 yr ALMA-JWST gap

evidence.quote: the expected displacement over this period is $\sim115$ AU (equivalent to $\sim0.22\ensuremath{''}$ at Orion distance 400 pc and inclination angle 40$\ensuremath{^\circ}$)

Systemic velocity and moment-map velocity ranges for CO and SiO
Exact H2 line fluxes, aperture position and the fitting procedure for the rotational diagram and A_V
Reconciliation of the conflicting N(H2) and A_V values
Gaussian fitting details for the ALMA SiO knot centroid and the WCS alignment between ALMA and JWST
score_reason: Both datasets are public and the JWST tool is released, with a clear ALMA calibration/imaging statement (CASA 6.5.4, robust +2.0, beams), but many imaging and rotational-diagram settings are missing and N(H2) values conflict.
rediscovery_reason: Public data in ALMA and MAST archives, released code, and numeric results (T1, T2, A_V, N(H2), mass-loss rate) allow a redo, although the missing aperture and fit details need choices.
